cues.text: Let's work through an archived pre-test revision set.
It contains three questions, numbered Q6, Q9 and Q10, and we will take them in that order.
Pre-test question six.
This one asks you to evaluate the role of the SELECT clause, which means recognising its primary function within an SQL query.
The question is: which of the following best describes this function?
Option one: to specify the columns or expressions to retrieve from a table.
Option two: to filter rows based on specific conditions.
Option three: to group data for aggregate calculations.
Option four: to define the order in which data is retrieved.
The archived LMS correct answer is option one: to specify the columns or expressions to retrieve from a table.
Pre-test question nine.
Here the focus is the optimisation process.
The question asks: which of the following best describes the significance of the parsing stage?
Option one: it applies statistical data to estimate query costs.
Option two: it validates the SQL syntax and creates a parse tree for further processing.
Option three: it executes the chosen query plan to retrieve data.
Option four: it generates multiple physical execution plans for evaluation.
The archived LMS correct answer is option two: it validates the SQL syntax and creates a parse tree for further processing.
Pre-test question ten.
This question investigates cost estimation factors and their influence on performance.
It asks: which of the following is most accurate regarding performance?
Option one: query complexity has no bearing on resource consumption.
Option two: disk I/O and memory usage significantly affect query execution time.
Option three: network latency is the primary concern in centralised databases.
Option four: CPU cost is irrelevant when indexes are present.
The archived LMS correct answer is option two: disk I/O and memory usage significantly affect query execution time.
Now let's look at the reasoning behind all three answers.
For question six, each SQL clause has its own job.
SELECT projects expressions, meaning it chooses what appears in the output.
WHERE filters rows.
GROUP BY groups rows together.
ORDER BY sorts the results.
So the distractors in that question describe WHERE, GROUP BY and ORDER BY in turn, and only the first option describes SELECT.
For question nine, the key idea is sequence: parsing precedes optimisation and execution.
Parsing comes first, checking the syntax and building the parse tree.
Only after that can the optimiser work, and only after optimisation is there a chosen plan to execute.
That is why the other options, which describe cost estimation, execution and plan generation, belong to later stages.
For question ten, I/O and memory costs are major factors alongside CPU, network and other resources.
In other words, disk I/O and memory usage matter a great deal, but they sit among several resources that contribute to cost.

That is why the claims that complexity has no bearing, that network latency is the primary concern in centralised databases, or that CPU cost is irrelevant with indexes, are not the most accurate statements.
